b: Good manners and proper conduct, with Allah and with people.
The call to prayer.
Words of remembrance said at set times, such as morning, evening and after prayer (singular dhikr).
The family of the Prophet ﷺ: his ﷺ wives, children and their descendants, and his ﷺ relatives from Banu Hashim.
The People of the Book: Jews and Christians.

f: What does 'Ahl al-Sunnah wa al-Jama'ah' mean?
b: The main body of Muslims who follow the Sunnah and the Companions. In belief: the Ash'ari and Maturidi schools.
The Hereafter: life after death, the Day of Judgement, Paradise and the Fire.
'The Helpers': the Muslims of Madinah who took in the Prophet ﷺ and the emigrants.
Belief: what a Muslim holds to be true in the heart about Allah, His Messengers and the unseen.
The sacrifice for a newborn, on the seventh day.
The school of belief of Imam Abu al-Hasan al-Ash'ari رحمه الله, followed by most Shafi'is and Malikis.
The part of the body that must be covered. In prayer, for a man from the navel to below the knees; for a woman all but the face, hands and feet.
Those who often turn back to Allah. Salat al-awwabin is six recommended rak'ahs after Maghrib.
A verse of the Qur'an; also a sign of Allah.
Having reached puberty, after which the religious duties become binding.
The life of the grave, between death and the Resurrection.
A pledge, as taken with a shaykh: a promise to keep to the Shari'ah and the practices of the path under his guidance.
An innovation in the religion with no basis in the Shari'ah.
'In the name of Allah': said before eating, entering, starting any good act.
A simple frame drum, allowed to announce a wedding and on the days of Eid.
A penalty sacrifice of a sheep or goat, owed for certain mistakes in Hajj, slaughtered in the Haram.
The short vowel 'u', a small waw above the letter.
Remembrance of Allah, with the tongue and the heart.
For liquid impurity, the size of the hollow of the palm (about 3 cm across). For solid impurity, a weight of a few grams.
Calling upon Allah, asking Him.
The forenoon, after the sun has risen well until shortly before midday; also the recommended prayer of that time, four rak'ahs or more in Nur al-Idah.
Obligatory, proven beyond doubt. Leaving it is a major sin; denying it is disbelief.
What every single Muslim must know and do, like the basics of belief, prayer and purity.
A communal obligation: if some Muslims do it, the rest are free of it; if nobody does it, everyone who could have is sinful. Example: the funeral prayer.
The short vowel 'a', a small line above the letter.
A ruling given by a qualified scholar (mufti) in answer to a question.
A payment of food for each fast someone cannot make up, such as the very old.
The rulings of worship and daily life: how to pray, fast, and so on.
Heavy impurity, such as urine, stools, flowing blood and wine. Only a small amount (a dirham) is excused.
The false oath: swearing by Allah about the past while knowing it is a lie. A major sin with no expiation but repentance.
Backbiting: saying something true about someone behind their back that they would dislike. A major sin.
The nasal sound from the nose, held about two counts, in nun and mim.
Washing the whole body, needed after janabah, menstruation and post-natal bleeding.
Custody: the right to raise young children, which goes first to the mother.
A report of what the Prophet ﷺ said, did or approved.
The narration of the Qur'an from Imam 'Asim through Hafs, the one most Muslims recite today.
The pilgrimage to Makkah, fard once in a lifetime for those able.
A spiritual state that comes over the heart as a gift and passes (plural ahwal).
Lawful, permitted.
A marriage arranged only to make a thrice-divorced woman lawful again to her first husband. The Prophet ﷺ cursed it.
The school of fiqh of Imam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله. The lessons follow it.
Forbidden. Doing it is a sin.
Menstruation: the monthly period. In the Hanafi school, 3 to 10 days.
The migration of the Prophet ﷺ from Makkah to Madinah, which begins the Islamic calendar.
Staying in the masjid with the intention of worship, especially the last ten nights of Ramadan.
The waiting period after divorce or death before a woman may remarry.
Merging one letter into the next.
Doing Hajj alone, without 'umrah.
Breaking the fast at sunset.
The state of a pilgrim, entered with the intention and the talbiyah; also the two white sheets men wear.
Worshipping Allah as if you see Him; and if you do not see Him, He sees you.
Consensus of the qualified scholars of the Ummah on a ruling.
Hiding a letter: saying it lightly through the nose, between clear and merged.
Sincerity: doing a deed for Allah alone.
Gesturing: praying the ruku' and sujud by bending the head, for someone too ill to make them, with sujud lower than ruku'.
The one who leads the prayer; also a title for a great scholar, such as Imam Abu Hanifah رحمه الله.
Faith: believing in the heart and declaring with the tongue.
The second call, said just before the prayer begins.
Turning a nun sakinah or tanween into a hidden mim before ba'.
The early Duha prayer, soon after sunrise once the forbidden time has passed.
A man making sure the urine has completely stopped before cleaning himself.
Calling on the Prophet ﷺ or the righteous for help, meaning: be my means to Allah and ask Him for me. Permissible, with the belief that Allah alone gives.
Bleeding outside the normal times of hayd and nifas. It does not stop prayer.
The prayer and du'a for asking Allah to choose what is best in a decision.
Cleaning the private parts after using the toilet, with water or with stones or tissue.
Saying the nun or mim clearly, without hiding or merging it.
Permissible: no sin in doing it or leaving it.
One of the three stone pillars at Mina that pilgrims throw pebbles at (plural jamarat).
The state after intercourse or a release of semen, which needs ghusl.
The funeral prayer, said standing, with four takbirs.
Beings created from smokeless fire, accountable like humans, some believers and some not.
The Friday prayer, two rak'ahs with a sermon, in place of Zuhr.
The House of Allah in Makkah, which Muslims face in prayer.
A major sin (plural kaba'ir): one with a specific threat of punishment, a curse or a legal penalty.
Suitability: the husband being a fitting match for the wife, mainly in religion and character.
An expiation for a serious wrong, such as breaking a Ramadan fast on purpose: 60 days of fasting in a row.
A soothsayer or fortune-teller who claims to know the unseen. Going to one is forbidden.
A wonder Allah does at the hands of one of His friends.
The short vowel 'i', a small line below the letter.
Light impurity, such as the urine of animals that are eaten. Less than a quarter of a garment or limb is excused.
Caliph: the leader of the Muslims after the Prophet ﷺ. The first four are Abu Bakr, 'Umar, 'Uthman and 'Ali رضي الله عنهم.
A man and a non-mahram woman being alone together where no one else can come in. It is forbidden.
An engagement: a promise to marry. It does not make the couple lawful to each other.
Leather socks covering the ankles, which may be wiped over in wudu for a set time.
A separation the wife asks for, giving back the mahr or something else for her release.
Humility and presence of heart in the prayer.
The sermon given by the imam, as on Friday and Eid.
The Night of Power in the last ten nights of Ramadan, better than a thousand months.
Musical instruments. Playing and choosing to listen to them is haram in the Hanafi school; the daff is allowed at weddings and on Eid.
Lengthening a long vowel: two counts naturally, up to six in some cases.
A school of fiqh, a tried way of understanding the rulings, such as the Hanafi school.
A thin, clear fluid that comes out with arousal, without spurts. It breaks wudu and must be washed off, but does not need ghusl.
Love of Allah, whose sign is following the Messenger ﷺ.
The marriage gift the husband owes the wife. It is her property alone.
A close relative a person can never marry, such as a parent, child or sibling. A woman travels with a mahram.
The point in the mouth or throat a letter comes from (plural makharij).
Disliked. Makruh tahriman is close to forbidden; makruh tanzihan is better left.

Prohibitively disliked (makruh tahrimi): close to haram. Doing it is a sin and deserves punishment, though less than haram, and whoever does it should repent. Its proof is not definitive, like wajib's. Examples: delaying 'Asr until the sun turns yellow, or praying while badly needing the toilet.

Mildly disliked (makruh tanzihi): better to leave. There is no sin in doing it, but leaving it is rewarded. Examples: yawning in prayer without covering the mouth, or praying bareheaded out of laziness.
Sexual fluid, which comes out with desire and in spurts. Its coming out with desire makes ghusl fard.
A spiritual station earned by effort that stays, such as repentance or patience (plural maqamat).
Wiping with a wet hand rather than washing, as over the head or over khuffs.
A mosque: a place set aside for the prayer.
The school of belief of Imam Abu Mansur al-Maturidi رحمه الله, followed by most Hanafis.
The birth of the Prophet ﷺ, and gatherings that remember it.
The boundary where pilgrims must enter ihram.
A weight of about 4.25 g (20 qirats), used for gold, a dirham's weight of solid impurity, and a man's silver ring.
The person who calls the adhan.
A miracle given to a Prophet to prove his prophethood.
Simply allowed, with no reward or sin either way.
'The Emigrants': the Muslims who left Makkah for Allah's sake and moved to Madinah.
Taking account of yourself: reviewing your deeds and repenting.
A person who has entered ihram.
A scholar able to derive rulings directly from the sources.
A person who is accountable: Muslim, sane and having reached puberty.
A resident: someone at home, or who intends to stay fifteen days or more in one place.
Watchfulness: knowing at every moment that Allah sees you.
A spiritual guide in the path of tazkiyah.
A traveller in the Shari'ah sense: someone who sets out intending a journey of about 78 km (48 miles) or more.
A written copy of the Qur'an. Wudu is needed to touch it.
Recommended: rewarded if done, no sin if left.
A vow: promising Allah an act of worship, such as a fast or charity. A valid vow must be fulfilled.
Maintenance: the food, clothing and housing a husband owes his wife, and a father his children.
A voluntary act of worship beyond what is required.
The self or ego, which inclines to desires and must be disciplined.
Impurity, such as urine, faeces or flowing blood. It must be washed off the body, clothes and place of prayer.
Impure: something that must be washed off the body, clothes or place of prayer before praying.
Tale-carrying: passing on what people say to stir up trouble between them.
The bleeding after giving birth. At most 40 days.
The minimum wealth on which zakat is due: about 87.5 g of gold or 612 g of silver, or the same value.
Intention: the purpose in the heart behind an act. Saying it with the tongue is not required.
The sitting in the prayer, for the tashahhud.
Making up a prayer or fast that was missed.
The decree: Allah knew, wrote and wills everything that happens.
A slight bounce on the letters ق ط ب ج د when they have a sukun.
Shortening the four-rak'ah prayers to two when travelling.
The direction of the Ka'bah in Makkah, which Muslims face in prayer.
Doing Hajj and 'umrah together in one ihram. The best form of Hajj in the Hanafi school.
The Day of Resurrection, when all are raised and judged.
Analogy: applying a ruling from the Qur'an or Sunnah to a new case with the same reason.
The three surahs that begin with 'Qul' (Say), recited for protection: al-Ikhlas (112), al-Falaq (113) and al-Nas (114), the last three surahs of the Qur'an.
The du'a said in the third rak'ah of witr, before bowing.
Nursing: a child nursed by a woman within the first two years becomes like her own child for marriage purposes.
A revocable divorce: after one or two talaqs the husband may take his wife back during the 'iddah.
One unit of the prayer: standing, reciting, bowing and two prostrations.
Walking briskly with short steps and moving shoulders in the first three circuits of tawaf, for men.
Interest or usury: an unlawful increase in a loan or in exchanging certain goods. A major sin.
Contentment with what Allah decrees.
Showing off: doing a deed to be seen by people.
Bowing in prayer, with hands on the knees.
Healing by reciting the Qur'an and prophetic du'as over someone.
Walking between Safa and Marwah seven times.
Patience: holding yourself to obedience, away from sin, and steady in hardship.
Charity given for Allah's sake, beyond what is required.
The Companions: Muslims who met the Prophet ﷺ and died as Muslims.
Two prostrations at the end of the prayer that repair a forgotten wajib.
The prostration of recitation: one prostration, wajib on whoever recites or hears one of the fourteen verses of prostration.
The prayer: the five daily prayers, with set times and actions.

Peace. In the prayer, the salam is saying 'al-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah', turning the face to the right and then to the left, which ends the prayer. As a greeting, it is the Muslim greeting of peace.
Sending blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ.
Fasting: no food, drink or intercourse from true dawn until sunset.

The master of seeking forgiveness, a du'a from Sahih al-Bukhari: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ، خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ، وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ، أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ، أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ، وَأَبُوءُ لَكَ بِذَنْبِي، فَاغْفِرْ لِي، فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ. O Allah, You are my Lord; there is no god but You. You created me and I am Your servant, and I keep Your covenant and promise as far as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge Your favour upon me, and I acknowledge my sin, so forgive me, for none forgives sins but You.
The life of the Prophet ﷺ.
A sign above a letter that doubles it.
Intercession: asking for good for others on the Day of Judgement, first of all by the Prophet ﷺ.
The testimony of faith: 'There is no god but Allah, and Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah.'
The sacred law: what Allah has commanded and forbidden.
Associating partners with Allah. The one sin Allah does not forgive if a person dies upon it.
Gratitude to Allah, with the heart, the tongue and the limbs.
Truthful in faith, word and deed. See Siddiqin.

The truthful ones (singular siddiq): the believers of the highest rank after the Prophets عليهم السلام, whose faith, words and deeds are wholly true. Abu Bakr al-Siddiq رضي الله عنه is their foremost. Allah lists them with the Prophets, the martyrs and the righteous (al-Nisa' 69).
Magic. It is real and harms only by Allah's permission; practising it is one of the seven destroying sins.
Keeping ties with relatives: a duty, and cutting them is a major sin.
The chain of teachers in a tariqah, going back to the Prophet ﷺ.
Companionship: keeping the company of a guide and the righteous for the sake of Allah.
The meal before dawn on a fasting day. A sunnah.
Prostration: forehead, nose, hands, knees and toes on the ground.
A small circle above a letter: it has no vowel.
The way of the Prophet ﷺ. As a ruling: something he ﷺ did regularly; rewarded, and leaving it without excuse is blameworthy.
A stressed sunnah: one the Prophet ﷺ did regularly. Leaving it now and then is not a sin, but making a habit of leaving it is blameworthy.
A chapter of the Qur'an. There are 114.

Seeking refuge in Allah before reciting: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ. A'udhu billahi min al-shaytan al-rajim: I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, the outcast. In the prayer it is said quietly after the thana', in the first rak'ah.
A written charm. One with only Qur'an, Allah's names or known du'as, believing that only Allah protects, is allowed by Hanafi scholars; charms believed to protect by themselves are shirk.
Explanation of the meanings of the Qur'an.
The voluntary night prayer, best in the last part of the night after some sleep.
Purity: being clean of impurity and in a state fit for prayer.
Pure: clean in the sense of the Shari'ah.
The rules for reciting the Qur'an correctly.
Saying 'Allahu akbar', Allah is the Greatest. The first takbir begins the prayer.
The opening 'Allahu akbar' that begins the prayer. After it, talking, eating and so on are forbidden until the salam.
Divorce pronounced by the husband.
The words said in ihram: 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk…' (Here I am, O Allah, here I am…).
Doing 'umrah in the months of Hajj, leaving ihram, then entering ihram again for Hajj in the same year.
A doubled vowel sign at the end of a word, adding an 'n' sound: -an, -in, -un.
Following a qualified scholar or school without knowing every proof yourself, as most people must.
God-consciousness: guarding yourself from Allah's displeasure by obeying Him and avoiding sin.
The sunnah night prayer of Ramadan, prayed after 'Isha'.
A Sufi path of purifying the heart under a guide, such as the Naqshbandi path.
The science of ihsan: purifying the heart and worshipping Allah as though you see Him, bound by the Book and the Sunnah.
Saying 'Subhan Allah' (Glory be to Allah); also the prayer beads used to count dhikr.
The words recited while sitting in prayer, bearing witness to Allah's Oneness and the Messenger ﷺ.
The days of tashriq: the 11th, 12th and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah.
Saying bismillah: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ, In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful.
Walking around the Ka'bah seven times.
Trust in Allah while still taking the means.
Asking Allah by means of something beloved to Him: His names, your good deeds, or the rank of the Prophet ﷺ and the righteous. Permissible.
Repentance: regret, stopping the sin, and resolving not to return.
The Oneness of Allah: in His Self, His attributes and His actions.
Purifying with clean earth when water cannot be used.
Purifying the heart of bad qualities and adorning it with good ones.

The opening praise, said straight after the first takbir: سُبْحَانَكَ اللَّهُمَّ وَبِحَمْدِكَ، وَتَبَارَكَ اسْمُكَ، وَتَعَالَى جَدُّكَ، وَلَا إِلَهَ غَيْرُكَ. Subhanaka Allahumma wa bi-hamdika, wa tabaraka smuka, wa ta'ala jadduka, wa la ilaha ghayruk: Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise. Blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god besides You.
The Eid al-Adha sacrifice (qurbani): wajib in the Hanafi school on everyone who owns the nisab.
The community of Muslims.
The lesser pilgrimage, which can be done at any time.
A thick white fluid that can come out after urinating. It breaks wudu like urine and is washed off.
Revelation from Allah to His prophets.
Necessary, but proven with a little less certainty than fard. Leaving it is a sin.
A close friend of Allah: a believer who is God-fearing.
The wedding meal held by the husband after the marriage: a sunnah.
Scrupulousness: staying away from what is doubtful out of fear of falling into the haram.
A daily set of dhikr, Qur'an and du'a that one keeps up regularly.
The odd-numbered prayer after 'Isha'. Wajib in the Hanafi school: three rak'ahs.
The washing before prayer: face, arms to the elbows, wiping the head, and feet to the ankles.
The yearly alms: 2.5% of wealth above the nisab, owned for a lunar year.
A small charity given before the Eid prayer at the end of Ramadan.
Detachment: not letting the world take hold of the heart, even while using it.
